message.content:
**Earliest historical references to Jesus Christ (outside the New Testament)**  

| Source | Date (approx.) | Passage & Significance |
|--------|----------------|------------------------|
| **Josephus – *Antiquities of the Jews*, Book 18, Chapter 3, Section 3** | 93–94 CE | “Now there was a wise man named Jesus, who was a doer of wonderful works… He was crucified by Pontius Pilate.”  This is the earliest surviving non‑Christian mention of Jesus, written about 20–30 years after his death. |
| **Tacitus – *Annals*, Book 15, Chapter 44** | 116 CE | “Christus, the founder of the name, was executed by Pontius Pilate during the reign of Tiberius.”  A Roman historian’s brief but clear reference to Jesus’ execution. |
| **Pliny the Younger – *Letters*, 10.96** | 112 CE | “The Christians worship Christ as a god.”  An early Roman official’s observation of Christian worship practices. |

**Earliest Christian literary reference**

- **Mark the Evangelist – *Gospel of Mark*** (c. 65–70 CE)  
  - Opening verse: “The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.”  
  - Mark is generally accepted as the first Gospel written, providing the earliest Christian narrative of Jesus’ life.

---

### Bottom line
The **earliest independent historical record** of Jesus Christ comes from **Josephus** in the early 90s CE. The earliest Christian text is **Mark’s Gospel** from the 60s–70s CE. Subsequent Roman sources (Tacitus, Pliny) confirm his existence and crucifixion a few decades later.
